changes: Scribe p2: residence changed from the place-of-copying phrase to 'khāranyamaṃ' (the word right before 'kāyhastha'; probably a house or locality name, reading uncertain); confidence lowered to low because the name breaks off after 'jayate'
Date: weekday normalized to Friday (bhṛguvāsara); era NS kept but flagged as inferred, since the colophon has only 'samvata'; ce_approx filled with the range for NS 400–499
Notes expanded: Yambu/Canigala, the uncertain 'khāranyamaṃ', the lost month, and the unclear closing words

notes: The year breaks off after '4' and the month name is lost in the lacuna. The era is not named. 'samvata' with a 4xx year, Newari script and a Kathmandu location point to Nepal Samvat (NS 400–499 = c. 1280–1379 CE), but the century is inferred. Yambu is the old name for northern Kathmandu. Canigala is unidentified, perhaps a tole of Kathmandu. 'Bramāyā(!)' is corrupt. 'khāranyamaṃ' stands before 'kāyhastha (= kāyastha) jayate///'. It is probably the scribe's house or locality name, though it could be part of his name. The scribe's name is cut off after 'Jayate-', so the full form (e.g. Jayateja…) is unknown. The closing 'lakṣmīputradve vṛ//' is unclear and may be a further blessing or a fragment of a name; it has not been treated as a person. The author 'bhūbhṛd Dilīpa' (King Dilīpa) is named only as the text's author, not as the reigning king of this copy.
